title: What is known about 1RB0LD_1LC0RE_---1LD_1LE1LA_1RA0LF_1LC1RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_1LC0RE_---1LD_1LE1LA_1RA0LF_1LC1RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the head's fast moves through the background and the halting situations (kernel), and no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide); the C simulator finds no halt in 109 steps.

What it does. The tape is the alternating pattern 1010… with defects: places where two equal cells meet (11, 111, 1111, 00). About 16% of neighbouring pairs are 11 and about 4% are 00, and these fractions hardly change as the tape grows. The head does not sweep cleanly: it crosses the tape in zig-zags of tens to hundreds of cells, moving the defects around, and no regular word or counter shows up.

Where a halt would come from. Only C reading a 0 halts. C is entered from B and from F reading a 0 (each writes a 1 and steps left), so 0 B>0 and 0 F>0 halt (halt_B, halt_F). In the run, whenever B or F reads a 0 the cell to its left is a 1.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 31,386 cells have been visited and 24,640 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.493).

claims.title: Every way to a halt
claims.text: Two steps before any halt the machine is in 0 0 E>1 (so 0 B>0 never happens: B is entered from A, which leaves a 1 on its left); no other configuration halts within three steps.

claims.title: Fast moves
claims.text: Moving right, A turns each 0101 of the background into 1101 and B turns each 1010 into 1011, eight steps a copy, for any number of copies.

claims.title: The halting situations
claims.text: 0 B>0 and 0 F>0 halt after two steps; these are the only ways into C reading a 0.

claims.title: Constant density of defects
claims.text: At the left-end turns the tape has 557 cells with 81 pairs 11 and 34 pairs 00 (step 324,106), 1,765 cells with 292 and 59 (step 2,938,156), 3,077 cells with 486 and 119 (step 9,176,284).

claims.title: Never close to halting
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>6</sup> steps B reads a 0 and F reads a 0 tens of thousands of times, always with a 1 to the left.

claims.title: Regular-language deciders tried (F11)
claims.text: None of these closes: each reaches a halting configuration in its abstraction, which says nothing about whether the machine halts. n-gram CPS (tools/c/ngramcps.c), equal widths on both sides: a halting local configuration is reached with plain up to width 20, history 1 up to width 20, history 2 up to width 20, history 3 up to width 20, LRU history up to width 11 (larger widths ran out of the 150 s or 60 million configuration budget). n-gram CPS with every cell tagged by its position mod p: fails for p = 2 up to width 20, p = 3 up to width 20, p = 4 up to width 16, p = 6 up to width 20. n-gram CPS where each side also carries the state of a small automaton that has read that side from the far end (every automaton with up to 3 states on both sides, or 4 states on one side), with position mod 1..4 and widths 4, 6, 8: no closed set without a halt in all 120 parameter sets. Run-length windows (the K nearest runs of equal macro cells on each side, run lengths kept exactly below T and mod M above): fails for all 72 parameter sets (cells of 1 to 4 bits, K = 2, 4, 6, T = 2, 4, M = 1, 2, 4). Two-automaton closed tape language by SAT (a deterministic automaton reading each side inward, n states each, CaDiCaL): no solution for n = 2..8; n = 9 not finished in 150 s.
claims.where: sweeps of 13 November 2026 (family F11); the tagged and run-length deciders are not in the repository yet

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. No macro structure has been found; the next step would be a finer description of how one zig-zag moves the defects, or a closed set of local patterns that excludes 0 B>0 and 0 F>0. Later.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. The tape is an alternating pattern full of defects, and the head shuffles them around without any order we have found. This page runs it in your browser.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 31,386 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Defects in an alternating background
html: Stop the simulator when the head turns at the left end and write x for a 0. A stretch of the tape at step 2,938,258 reads
B>1 x x 1 x 1 1 1 x 1 x 1 x 1 x 1 x 1 1 x 1 x 1 x 1 x 1 x 1 x 1 1 x 1 x 1 x 1 x 1 1 1 x 1 x x 1 ...

Mostly 1 x 1 x, the alternating background, with defects: 1 1, 1 1 1, x x. Counting pairs of equal neighbours at the left-end turns, about one pair in six is 11 and one in twenty-five is 00, from the first thousand steps up to 107 (3,077 cells, 486 and 119 pairs). The positions of the defects show no repeating word.

The head moves through the background quickly: moving right, A turns 0101 0101 into 1101 1101 in sixteen steps (fill_A), and B does the same for 1010 (fill_B). At the defects it turns around, so a crossing of the tape is a long irregular zig-zag rather than a sweep.

The only halt is C reading a 0, reached from 0 B>0 or 0 F>0 (halt_B, halt_F). In the run the cell to the left of B or F is a 1 whenever they read a 0. Without a macro description there is no invariant yet; this machine is left for later.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.493).
After 109 steps the tape spans 31,386 cells (17,207 left of the start, 5,946 right), with a density of 1s of 0.785.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: alternating background with disordered defects (no visible macro structure)
summary: An alternating background 1010... sprinkled with defects (11, 111, 00) at a roughly constant density; the head moves through it in irregular zig-zags and the arrangement of defects looks disordered. Open.
